This opaque terminal feedback severely limits the interpretability of the search process itself, offering no insight into why a candidate succeeds or fails. Consequently, reusable structures in otherwise suboptimal candidates are often discarded, whereas incidental syntax along successful search trajectories may be repeatedly reinforced. We propose SED-MCTS, a Monte Carlo tree search approach that distills structural experience from evaluated expressions and reuses it to guide subsequent symbolic solution search. Across a diverse suite of PDE benchmarks, SED-MCTS achieves strong performance under a fixed evaluation budget and improves search efficiency and robustness under noisy or scarce observations. article.body:
SED-MCTS uses counterfactual subtrees to guide PDE solution search

SED-MCTS applies Monte Carlo tree search to discover symbolic expressions for physical fields from observations and known physical constraints. It addresses a limitation of terminal-score feedback: a single score for data fidelity and physical consistency does not reveal which subexpressions help or hurt a candidate.

The method uses counterfactual subtree interventions to estimate local structural contributions, routes reliable evidence to construction edges and stores useful components in a structural archive for later searches.

The authors report results across a suite of PDE benchmarks, with improved search efficiency and robustness under noisy or scarce observations at a fixed evaluation budget. The available abstract gives no benchmark names, metrics, numerical gains or detailed baseline comparisons, limiting assessment of the reported improvements.
